clue.text: Guards marking time

definitions.meaning: keeps an eye on, as sentries and lookouts do
devices worn on the wrist that tell the hour

explanation.surface: Sentries mark time on parade, standing still until relieved.
explanation.definitionFit: To guard is to keep vigil over something, and the timepieces on a wrist register the hours; one word covers the verb and the plural noun.

clue.text: They tighten nuts in cleaning machines

definitions.meaning: flat rings fitted under nuts to make them grip

explanation.surface: Seals that grip bolts inside laundry appliances.
explanation.definitionFit: Small metal rings seat a nut firmly on a bolt, and dishwashers and laundry machines are also named for the cleaning they do.

clue.text: Beat fellow to the line

parts.note: to tan someone's hide is to beat them
a gent is a fellow, a man

explanation.surface: A man wins a race by beating another to the finishing line.
explanation.walkthrough: The geometric line touches a curve at one point.
explanation.definitionFit: In geometry it is a straight line touching a curve at a single point.

clue.text: Take oneself off when there's a strike about work

indicators.note: the strike goes about, around, the short word for work

parts.note: to strike is to hit
op is short for opus, a work

explanation.surface: Workers walk out when a strike is called over a job.
explanation.walkthrough: 'strike' suggests industrial action; it is simply HIT.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase is slang for go away, clear off.

clue.text: The alarm must be to start the job

definitions.meaning: an alarm clock has to be set so it will function
to begin working on a task

explanation.surface: The alarm needs setting before the working day starts.
explanation.definitionFit: An alarm adjusted so it will operate is ready to function, and to get going on a task is to begin labouring.

clue.text: Animal in a role that gives limited protection

indicators.note: the animal sits inside the word for a role, between its third and fourth letters

parts.note: a role in a play is a part
an ape is an animal

explanation.surface: An actor cast as an animal finds the costume does little to shield them.
explanation.definitionFit: A low wall along a roof or bridge edge only partly shields those behind it, so it is a limited safeguard.

clue.text: Capital fighter in the Trojan war

definitions.meaning: the Trojan prince whose abduction of Helen began the war

explanation.surface: A capital fellow fighting at Troy.
explanation.definitionFit: It is the French capital, and the Trojan prince who carried off Helen and later killed Achilles.

clue.text: Miners get formed into militant groups

indicators.note: the letters are formed into a new arrangement

explanation.surface: Striking pit workers organise into militant bands.
explanation.walkthrough: 'formed into' suggests the miners organising; 'formed' is the anagram signal on MINERS GET.
explanation.definitionFit: Army units of soldiers are military bodies, so militant groups in the martial sense.

clue.text: Looking more sickly, goes to doctor in Sicily

indicators.note: the first part goes to, is joined by, the doctor

parts.note: looking more sickly means paler
MO is a medical officer, a doctor

explanation.surface: Someone feeling worse sees a doctor while on holiday in Sicily.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is minimal: a place that is in Sicily, its capital.
explanation.definitionFit: It is the capital city of the island of Sicily.

clue.text: Travelling goods will be in it

definitions.text: Travelling goods will be in it

parts.words: Travelling goods will be in it
parts.note: goods on the move are said to be in this state, being conveyed

explanation.surface: A van carrying freight.
explanation.definitionFit: Merchandise being carried from place to place is in conveyance, on its way.

clue.text: Young players may end up in this bunker

definitions.text: Young players may end up in this bunker

parts.words: Young players may end up in this bunker
parts.note: children at play end up in a box of sand, which is also what a golfer's bunker is

explanation.surface: Junior golfers keep finding the bunker.
explanation.walkthrough: The young players are not golfers but small children; the 'bunker' is the playground box of sand they dig in.
explanation.definitionFit: A playground box filled with sand resembles a golf course's sand trap, the hazard golfers call a bunker.

clue.text: Royal symbols from Algeria

indicators.note: the letters are made from the country's name, rearranged into a new word

explanation.surface: Crown jewels have been brought over from North Africa.
explanation.walkthrough: 'from' is the anagram signal: the letters are formed out of ALGERIA.
explanation.definitionFit: Crowns, sceptres and orbs are the emblems of monarchy worn or carried at coronations.

clue.text: Ballots to silence discord

indicators.note: discord means the letters fall out of harmony and are jumbled

explanation.surface: Votes are held to put an end to quarrelling.
explanation.walkthrough: 'discord' looks like the thing being silenced, but it tells you to scramble TO SILENCE.
explanation.definitionFit: Polls in which people vote are ballots.

clue.text: Targets given by teachers for work

definitions.meaning: things aimed at, as a mark is
grades or scores awarded to pupils' work

explanation.surface: Teachers set goals and then grade the homework.
explanation.definitionFit: A mark is something aimed at, and teachers award scores out of ten or a hundred for schoolwork.

clue.text: Located by eye and ear?

indicators.note: the question mark and the ear say the word is heard, not seen

parts.note: seen by eye means sighted

explanation.surface: Something found by looking and listening.
explanation.walkthrough: SIGHTED (found by eye) heard by ear sounds like SITED.
explanation.definitionFit: Something placed or positioned somewhere is situated there.

clue.text: Maddening disposition of the importunate

indicators.note: a disposition is an arrangement, so the letters are arranged afresh

explanation.surface: The persistent pester with maddening temperament.
explanation.walkthrough: 'disposition' suggests temperament; it means arrangement, rearranging MADDENING.
explanation.definitionFit: Importunate means persistently pressing in requests, insistent.

clue.text: Emphatically not at home

definitions.meaning: thoroughly, completely, as in a total rogue
absent twice over, gone and gone

explanation.surface: A firm statement that nobody is in.
explanation.walkthrough: Someone not at home is OUT; the phrase doubles it.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase means utterly or complete, an emphatic intensifier, and read literally it repeats the word for being away from the house.

clue.text: A roundabout way to come in

definitions.text: A roundabout way to come in

parts.words: A roundabout way to come in
parts.note: a rotating barrier at a stadium entrance literally turns round as you pass through

explanation.surface: An indirect route of entry.
explanation.walkthrough: 'roundabout' means indirect in the surface but here describes a gate that revolves.
explanation.definitionFit: A revolving gate with arms admits one person at a time at stadiums and stations.

clue.text: He has found a job at last

definitions.text: He has found a job at last

parts.words: He has found a job at last
parts.note: a last is the foot-shaped block a cobbler works on, so his job is literally at a last

explanation.surface: A man celebrates landing work after a long search.
explanation.walkthrough: 'at last' seems to mean finally; a last is the wooden foot-form on which boots are made.
explanation.definitionFit: A cobbler shapes footwear around a wooden last, so his trade is done at one.

clue.text: Ruin a runaway affair on ship

definitions.meaning: to wreck or sink a plan
an opening in a deck's edge letting water run away overboard

explanation.surface: An elopement aboard ship goes disastrously wrong.
explanation.walkthrough: 'runaway affair' suggests an elopement; it is a drain through which water runs away off the deck.
explanation.definitionFit: To wreck a scheme is to sink it, and a ship's drainage hole at deck level lets water escape overboard.

clue.text: Inauspicious for returning doctor — one with commonsense

indicators.note: returning means the doctor's letters are read backwards

parts.note: MO is a medical officer, a doctor
I is the Roman numeral one
nous is common sense

explanation.surface: Bad omens for a doctor coming back, but one with sense.
explanation.definitionFit: Threatening and foreboding, it is unfavourable as an omen.

clue.text: Faces the teams

definitions.meaning: surfaces of a solid, as a cube has six
the opposing parties in a match

explanation.surface: Confronting the opposing squads.
explanation.definitionFit: A cube's flat surfaces are its faces, and the two opposing elevens in a game are the two halves of the contest.

clue.text: Lengthen transvestite apparel no longer in fashion?

parts.note: drag is clothing of the opposite sex
out means unfashionable

explanation.surface: Cross-dressing outfits have gone out of fashion.
explanation.definitionFit: To prolong a meeting or story is to stretch it, make it last longer.

clue.text: Poet with no saving graces?

definitions.meaning: Stephen, the twentieth-century English poet of the Auden circle
one who saves nothing, a wastrel with money

explanation.surface: A poet utterly lacking in redeeming qualities.
explanation.walkthrough: 'saving graces' suggests virtues; read literally it is someone who never saves.
explanation.definitionFit: Stephen of that name was a British poet, and someone who never puts money by is a free user of cash.

clue.text: University running student organisation

parts.note: a machine that is running is on

explanation.surface: A university is running a club for its students.
explanation.definitionFit: The students' union is the representative body of a college's student population.

clue.text: Assume mail delayed about mid-January

indicators.note: the post and the late letters are put about, around, the January middle

parts.note: mail is post
delayed means late
the middle letter of the seven in January is U

explanation.surface: Expect the post to be late around the middle of January.
explanation.definitionFit: To put forward a premise as true without proof is to take it for granted.

clue.text: Writer writing odes, perhaps

parts.note: Edgar Allan Poe, the American writer
MS is a manuscript, a piece of writing

explanation.surface: An author writing some odes.
explanation.definitionFit: Odes are one kind of verse composition, examples of the wider class.

clue.text: We object to long period of employment

parts.note: us is the object form of we
an age is a long period

explanation.surface: We protest against a long spell of work.
explanation.walkthrough: 'object' seems a verb of protest; it is grammar, the objective case of 'we'.
explanation.definitionFit: Use or application of something is how it is put to work.

clue.text: Brief biography of professional record holder

parts.note: pro is short for professional
a file holds records

explanation.surface: A short life story of a champion athlete.
explanation.walkthrough: 'record holder' suggests a champion; it is a folder holding documents.
explanation.definitionFit: A short descriptive article about a person, as in a newspaper, is a pen portrait.

clue.text: Briefly, I draw no new conclusion

indicators.note: giving the letters a new conclusion, a fresh outcome, means rearranging them

explanation.surface: Put shortly, I reach no fresh verdict.
explanation.walkthrough: 'new conclusion' tells you to rearrange I DRAW NO.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase means in short, summed up with a single term.

clue.text: Son breaks rules, quits

indicators.note: the son breaks into the word for rules, splitting it

parts.note: a monarch rules or reigns

explanation.surface: A son flouts the regulations and walks out.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rules' looks like a noun but is the verb reigns.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who gives up a post steps down from it.

clue.text: English clergyman and builder

parts.note: a rector is a parish clergyman

explanation.surface: An English vicar who also does building work.
explanation.definitionFit: One who puts up structures raises them, which is what a builder does.
